What should I do about the width of the opening...?
Since it's short, I should make it as narrow as possible...

Today... I should be able to make two. Time-wise, using quick-drying
mortar for quick prototypes is probably the limit. One with a base, and a rectangular prism...
No, Grandpa's work has... much finer, smoother lines.

Due to days of prototyping, the materials she brought to the training camp were dwindling.
Worrying about the remaining materials might break her concentration.
—Right, flowers...

No.
What I brought wasn't enough.
............If you like it that much, you can have it.
Um... so, that. It's my way of saying thanks.

She wasn't in the middle of training, nor did she seem to have
any duties, so Believe could probably lend a hand, but...

Besides, the water ripple pattern I drew this time is a simple one.
I still can't draw patterns as intricate as that...
I won't... help out with that. Nor will I call out to her.
...It's a very standard ripple pattern.

—Surely, she had become able to craft something satisfying enough
to feel ready to show her grandfather.

A beautiful, teardrop-shaped single-flower vase. With a clover inserted,
its simple yet refined, flowing pattern stood out even more vividly.

She seemed completely engrossed in it. Lately, she appeared
to be repeatedly making prototypes over and over.

The festival is tomorrow, right?
The Trainer said it's fine for us to go, so why don't you come along too?

A little while ago, when we visited her grandparents' house,
she learned how to craft mortar single-flower vases from her grandfather—

Being able to watch her proud gaze and beautiful "work" by her side—
that in itself felt like an irreplaceable, precious luxury.
————Done.

I just want to quietly watch over her... and let her focus
on her "work" to her heart's content. To that end, too—

(The shape... is well-balanced too. The mortar hardened cleanly.
The pattern is... the best one yet.)

Thank you for your hard work.
...Well then, I'll take my leave.

The mortar... increased.
It was you, wasn't it, Trainer?
............Once I make one more, to Grandpa—
............It was a big help..

During summer camp, everyone usually enjoys seaside activities,
local festivals, and fireworks shows in addition to training.

(Speaking of single-flower vase designs... egg shape, teardrop shape... ring shape...
—Whoa... this one combines slabs to depict petals.)

No—
..................I will hone my craft further.
............You can take a look, if you want.

Huh, really?
Thank you so much!

Refreshing themselves that way helps them dedicate themselves
more to training. However—

It doesn't matter. I plan to make several more anyway.
Besides...

Though she spoke with composure, her expression as she looked at the vase
seemed thoroughly satisfied with the craftsmanship, carrying a hint of pride...
————Yeah. It's beautiful.

(............There are quite a few plaster artists out there.
I need to look at more works and broaden my range...)

I had only intended to watch quietly, but I ended up speaking out loud.
I thought I should leave right away, but... I'm curious about Believe's work...

Please let her use that space during free time—
I went around asking every staff member and Trainer at the academy.

She noticed... To call this "supporting from the shadows,"
I'm still quite inexperienced, or rather...

Hey hey, wanna play beach volleyball after this?
Let's invite those girls too!

(Rounded shapes are difficult, aren't they...?
Still, the cubes have gotten quite consistent, so it's about time...)

Believe paid no heed whatsoever to such recreation,
completely absorbed in a certain task.

This will do for now...
The length should be... about this much.

Ah! Believe-chan's Trainer! We're preparing for the recreation
activities right now, but we're short-handed. Is she free?

The grove out back? Ah, now that you mention it, I do spot
that trainee of yours around there quite often.

............All right.
Let's try... an egg shape.

Sure thing. She seems quite focused, so
I'll let everyone know not to unnecessarily disturb her.

Holding it in my hands to look closely... I'm thoroughly enchanted all over again.
Even to an amateur's eye, it's clear this is superior to any previous prototype.

Meticulous, flawless, and beautiful. Precisely because of its simple design,
the refined strokes are evident. Her grandfather's work was also pinnacle craftsmanship, but—

Thus, Believe spent almost all her free time every day
crafting single-flower vases. Continuing to watch over her—

The place Believe worked in was an area not used for training,
a deserted corner of the grove where hardly any students ventured.
